Good question. With the current API provided by Godot - a boolean property - I think it probably only makes sense to use the main window. If for example a game has a settings window where this setting can be toggled, it would be wrong to attach the inhibit request to that settings window, because then the inhibit would be cancelled when the settings window closes.
So I guess that means I should change the X11 code to match. Currently it attaches the inhibit request to the last focused window.
Yes, using main windows would make more sense in this case.

To my considerable surprise, the [specification](https://flatpak.github.io/xdg-desktop-portal/docs/doc-org.freedesktop.portal.Inhibit.html#org-freedesktop-portal-inhibit-inhibit) doesn't document the semantics I had assumed, and the window ID parameter is actually completely unused by the two major portal backends (GTK and KDE). I have opened a discussion about [documenting what the semantics should be](https://github.com/flatpak/xdg-desktop-portal/discussions/1837) but I think for the time being the simple thing to do is to use the main window ID in both code paths.

I don't think it will prevent future requests, because each display server keeps its own track of whether it has tried to inhibit the screensaver, and will only make an `inhibit()` request if it believes the current state is uninhibited (and vice versa). So if:

- game calls `DisplayServer.screen_set_keep_on(true)`
- the request fails
- game calls `DisplayServer.screen_set_keep_on(true)` again

by design nothing will happen, just as if the request hadn't failed.

If:

- game calls `DisplayServer.screen_set_keep_on(true)`
- it fails
- game calls `DisplayServer.screen_set_keep_on(false)`

the failed request will be cleaned up (just as if it had succeeded) and you can call `DisplayServer.screen_set_keep_on(true)` again later.
(As a practical matter, neither the GTK nor KDE backends seem to report errors on any codepath...)
